story.what_it_does: eClerx is a services company that earns revenue from delivering data, analytics, automation and operations work to clients, with many in financial services (BFSI), fashion and luxury, and retail. It delivers much of this from offshore centres and is pushing into agentic AI and analytics. FY26 revenue was Rs 41,170 million, up about 22%.
story.plans: Management targets top-quartile revenue growth versus peers in FY27 and an EBITDA margin band of 24% to 28%. It plans about Rs 130 crore of capex for FY27 and expects agentic AI win deployments and a BFSI turnaround, though the BFSI timing has slipped to Q4 FY27. It declined to give a numeric growth forecast.
story.moat: The notes show no explicit moat statement, but they point to long client relationships and scale: top ten clients gave about 60% of revenue and the company has had 13 straight quarters of sequential growth. Pressure on this position shows up as rising deal pricing competition, possible AI-driven deflation in contract values, and tighter client budgets.

scenarios.story: Deployments from agentic AI wins and a BFSI recovery lift growth, and the company meets its top-quartile growth goal. Margins recover toward the middle of the 24% to 28% band as investment and wage costs are absorbed.
signals_to_watch: BFSI growth turnaround arriving in Q4 FY27 as now guided
Agentic AI win deployments converting into revenue and new deal wins

scenarios.story: Revenue keeps rising sequentially at a modest pace, with USD growth slowing to around 10% to 13%. Margins stay near the low end of the 24% to 28% band while clients remain selective.
signals_to_watch: Operating EBITDA margin staying at or above 24% for the full year FY27
Seasonal bounce back in luxury in Q3 FY27

scenarios.story: Smaller AI pilot deals, pricing pressure and lower refresh volumes at existing clients keep slowing growth, while costs and attrition rise faster than revenue. Margins could slip below the 24% floor and profit growth lags revenue.
signals_to_watch: Annual contract value (ACV) falling short of last year's level, already down about 10% and described as difficult to match
Attrition (23.4% in Q2 FY27) and headcount growing faster than revenue
